title: Easy to criticize, hard to create: build with humility instead of trying to be right
summary: Jason Cohen argues that tearing apart any business idea is trivial and useless, since the entrepreneur's job is to build, learn and stay humble rather than be right. He also warns against dismissing criticism wholesale, and suggests asking whether a sting hides a truth you don't want to face.

principles.text: Criticizing a business is easy and useless; betting against every startup makes you right often but ensures nothing new is created.
principles.quote: I suppose if your goal in life is to be *right*, you should bet against every startup, certainly against any novel ideas. You'll be right much more often than wrong.

principles.text: The entrepreneur's goal is not to be right but to build with humility, hold strong opinions while seeking better ones, and admit mistakes before they're fatal.
principles.quote: It's to construct with humility. To have strong opinions but seek better ones. To infect customers and employees with your peculiar disease. To live to fight another day. To acknowledge being wrong before the fault turns fatal.

principles.text: Treat startups like science: generate many ideas, expect most to be wrong, and don't get attached to a single one.
principles.quote: Real science is mostly being wrong, but staying vigilant and honest enough to continue being wrong until you're not wrong. So it is with dating. Or startups.

principles.text: A "failed" venture is never really a failure; founders come out with new skills, clarity on what motivates them, and more confidence.
principles.quote: I've never met a "failed" entrepreneur who doesn't proudly declare they're better off now: developed skills they never thought possible, learned what makes them excited to get up in the morning

principles.text: Builders must temper wanting to be right with shipping: ship before it's ready, even with bugs, and build what customers want.
principles.quote: Programmers want to be "right," but have to temper that with getting things built and shipped, even before it's ready, even with bugs

principles.text: Listen to critics with half an ear, but don't dismiss criticism without consideration; ask whether the sting reveals a truth you're avoiding.
principles.quote: Ignore the messenger, ignore the emotion, and see whether it's a gift of truth, poorly wrapped.
